## Screen: Deployment proposals (`hikvision-deployment-plans`, `deployment-plans.ts`)

**Purpose (end-user)**: For the currently selected, saved schedule draft, bind explicit device resource IDs (template / weekly plan / holiday group / holiday plans) on a chosen station, run a read-only comparison of what the station currently has at those IDs, and save it as a local "proposal" that reserves those IDs inside WisKey. Intro `plan_intro`: "Prepare and compare a proposed station configuration. Saving reserves these IDs only within this Home Assistant library; it does not establish device ownership or apply permissions." Every report shows `plan_not_applied`: "Not applied. Deployment and user assignment remain unavailable."

**Entry point**: rendered inside `hikvision-intercom-schedules` (`schedules.ts:1234-1241`) with `.hass .stations .source`. Emits `plan-busy` (CustomEvent<boolean>, bubbles/composed) so the parent disables its editor (`deployment-plans.ts:188-193`). Renders `<hikvision-schedule-operations .hass .stations .plans=${_items}>` below itself (`:516-520`).

**Layout & visual notes** (`deployment-plans.ts:369-521`):
- Section: title, intro, error/notice, Reload.
- If `source.id` (saved draft): form with legend = draft name; station select (lock-enabled only, offline disabled); hint `plan_binding_hint`; numeric inputs (1..65535, step 1) Template ID, Weekly ID, Holiday group ID (only if draft has holidays), one "Holiday ID n — <holiday name> (<start>)" per draft holiday; submit "Prepare" (shows `loading`). Otherwise text `plan_save_source`.
- Two-column `.fields` grid collapsing to one column < 600 px.
- Review section (after prepare): report + "Save proposal".
- Saved list: `<details>` per proposal (summary: name · station); report; Recheck (only if station online+lock), Export, "Delete local".
- Report block (`:339-368`): station name · checked_at in station zone; `plan_source_<current|changed|missing|unavailable>` · draft revision; drift list (danger); per resource row: kind #id · `plan_state_<matches|different|not_observed|unreadable|unsupported>`; coverage · "external reference" yes/no/—; changed fields list (`plan_field_<field>`); `plan_not_applied`; blockers list.
- Unknown-outcome lock `_uncertain` → `plan_unknown` ("The local save result is unconfirmed. Reload proposals before another change; no automatic retry was sent.").

**Data model** (`deployment-plans.ts:10-41`):
```ts
interface Source { id?: string; revision?: number; name: string; holidays: { name: string; start: string; end: string }[] }
interface Proposal { id: string; revision: number; station_id: string; draft_id: string; draft_revision: number; name: string;
  token?: string; source_state: string; drifted_resources: string[];
  bindings: { template: number; weekly: number; holiday_group: number | null; holidays: number[] };
  report: { checked_at: string; can_apply: false; blockers: string[];
    resources: { kind: string; id: number; coverage: string; state: string; fields: string[]; active: boolean | null; externally_referenced: boolean | null }[] } }
```
Backend also returns `created_at`, `can_apply:false`, `report.users:{state,error,read,explicit,implicit,malformed}`, and (preview/export only) `candidates:[{key, kind, id, dependencies, body}]`.

**User actions** (all via `api(command)` → `hikvision_intercom/schedules/plan_${command}`, timeout 120 s for preview/recheck else 60 s, `:194-199`)

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Load / Reload | READ (storage) | `schedules/plan_list` `{}` → Proposal[] | auto; also on `source` change | `:209-226` |
| Prepare (compare) | READ (device: full schedule inventory search + UserInfo search; in-memory 5-min pending token) | `schedules/plan_preview` `{station_id, schedule_id:<source.id>, revision:<source.revision>, bindings:{template:int, weekly:int, holiday_group:int\|null, holidays:int[]}}` | client validates IDs `^[1-9][0-9]{0,4}$` ≤65535 else `schedule_binding_invalid` | `:232-261` |

| Recheck | READ (device re-read) + CONFIG-WRITE of the stored report/revision/drift (storage only) | `schedules/plan_recheck` `{plan_id, revision}` | station must be online/lock-enabled | `:491-495` |
| Export | READ (storage) | `schedules/plan_export` `{plan_id, revision}` → proposal with `candidates` + `source_state`; downloaded `hikvision-deployment-proposal.json` | — | `:321-338` |

No station configuration will be changed." | `:262-264`, `:501-506` |

## Screen: Schedule operations (`hikvision-schedule-operations`, `schedule-operations.ts`)

**Purpose (end-user)**: Declare local "management responsibility" (claims) for the device resources of a saved proposal, create a per-proposal job, run background read-only preflight checks per station, cancel/archive jobs; view write-ahead journal status. Intro `operations_intro`: "Record management responsibility, prepare a job and check each station in the background. Schedule writes remain unavailable until verified on the device." Backend always returns `writes_enabled: false`.

**Entry point**: inside `hikvision-deployment-plans` (`deployment-plans.ts:516-520`) with `.plans` = saved proposals.

**Layout & visual notes** (`schedule-operations.ts:342-432`):
- Title, intro, error, Reload, Export (downloads `hikvision-schedule-operations.json`).
- Plan select (name · station), buttons "Preview claim" and "Create job".
- Claim review section: warning `operations_claim_warning` ("This local declaration records your responsibility for these resources. Existing references and unknown device defaults still block deployment. It does not establish that a slot is unused."), resource keys, blockers list, "Confirm claim".
- Claims list (`<details>` station · keys) with warning + "Release".
- Jobs list: `<details>` summary name · station · `operations_state_<status>`; plan revision · updated_at; ownership `operations_owner_<not_checked|missing|current|changed>`; resource keys; last check time; error; blockers; journal status `operations_journal_<status>` and steps `key — operations_step_<state>`; buttons Check, Cancel, Archive.
- Archive `<details>` (count) listing archived jobs without buttons.
- Unknown-outcome lock `_uncertain` → `operations_unknown` ("The response was lost. Reload the list before taking another action.").

**Data model** (`schedule-operations.ts:9-56`):
```ts
interface Plan { id: string; revision: number; name: string; station_id: string }
interface Claim { id: string; revision: number; plan_id: string; station_id: string; resource_keys: string[] }  // backend adds created_at
interface Job { id: string; revision: number; plan_id: string; plan_revision: number; station_id: string; name: string;
  resource_keys: string[]; status: string; error: string | null; blockers: string[]; ownership: string;
  journal_id: string | null; updated_at: string; report: { checked_at: string } | null }  // backend: full report, created_at
interface Workspace { claims: Claim[]; jobs: Job[]; archive: Job[];
  journal: { id: string; status: string; issue: string | null; steps: { key: string; state: string; attempted: boolean }[] }[];  // backend adds revision, created_at, updated_at
  writes_enabled: false }
interface ClaimReview { token: string; resource_keys: string[]; plan_id: string; plan_revision: number; report: { blockers: string[] } }
```
Resource key format `"<kind>:<id>"`, kind ∈ `template|weekly|holiday_group|holiday`.

**User actions** (type `hikvision_intercom/schedules/operations_${action}`, default 60 s timeout)

| Action | Classification | Command(s) | Confirmation / guard UX | file:line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Load / Reload / poll | READ (storage) | `schedules/operations_list` `{}` → Workspace | auto; polls every 1.5 s while any job queued/checking | `:184-213` |
| Export | READ (storage) | `schedules/operations_export` `{}` (identical payload to list) | — | `:352-357` |
| Preview claim | READ (device full inventory + users read; 5-min in-memory token) | `schedules/operations_claim_preview` `{plan_id, revision}` → ClaimReview | — | `:374-378` |
| Confirm claim | CONFIG-WRITE (storage `schedule_operations.claims` only) | `schedules/operations_claim_confirm` `{token}` | review section with warning | `:395-400` |
| Release claim | CONFIG-WRITE (storage only) | `schedules/operations_claim_release` `{claim_id, revision}` → `{released:true}` | `confirm(operations_release_confirm)`: "Release this local declaration? The station configuration will not be changed." | `:412-420` |
| Create job | CONFIG-WRITE (storage only; status `pending`) | `schedules/operations_create` `{plan_id, revision}` → Job | — | `:379-384` |
| Check (preflight) | READ (device, background task) + CONFIG-WRITE (storage: job status/report; may create a journal transaction in `schedule_journal`) | `schedules/operations_check` `{job_id, revision}` → Job (status `queued`) | disabled for queued/checking/cancelled/verified | `:317-322` |
| Cancel job | CONFIG-WRITE (storage; discards an unstarted journal transaction) | `schedules/operations_cancel` `{job_id, revision}` → Job (status `cancelled`) | `confirm(operations_cancel_confirm)`: "Cancel this local job? Any journal with an attempted write must be retained for recovery." | `:323-331` |
| Archive job | CONFIG-WRITE (storage) | `schedules/operations_archive` `{job_id, revision}` → `{archived:true}` | only cancelled/verified | `:332-337` |

# BACKEND MODULES

## Module: `technical_api.py`

**Responsibility**: Dispatcher for all `stations/technical_*` commands (door parameters, relay mapping, public codes, hold-open drafts, HA door programs) with an allowlist; no arbitrary URL passthrough.

**Common guard** (`:20-31`, `:200-204`): config entry must be this domain and loaded (`station_unloaded`); per-entry busy set `hass.data[DOMAIN]["technical_busy"]` — same station already busy, or ≥3 stations busy → `device_busy`; whole command under `asyncio.timeout(75)` (timeout → generic `action_failed`); after completion, entry reload/close → `station_unloaded`.

**Commands handled**

| Command | Input fields | Output | Classification | Permission | file:line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stations/technical_get` | `station_id:str` | `{checked_at, doors:[{door:1/2, values:{doorName?, openDuration?, relayReverseEnabled?}, constraints:{<field>:{type:"text"/"integer", min, max} or {type:"boolean"}}} or {door, error:<code>}], passwords:null or {states:{<PASSWORD_FIELDS>:bool/null}, public_pin_state:"configured"/"absent"/"unknown"}, password_error:null/<code>, features:[{family:"AccessControl"/"VideoIntercom", name:"isSupport…", supported:bool}], relay_selection:<entry.data.locks>}` | READ (device) | stations:view | `:151-199` |
| `stations/technical_update` | `station_id, door:int (API id, must be a managed api_id), expected:dict (current values), changes:dict (subset of doorName/openDuration/relayReverseEnabled), confirmed:bool (must be true)` | `{door, values, constraints}` read back | CONFIG-WRITE device (DoorParam); relay reverse may change physical lock state | stations:manage | `:145-150` → `client/technical.py:99-144` |
| `stations/technical_relays` | `station_id, expected:list (must equal entry.data.locks), locks:list[{physical_index:1/2, api_id:1/2, confirmed:true, name?:str 1..64}]` (≤2, unique) | `{reload_required:true}` | CONFIG-WRITE (HA config entry only; entry reload scheduled) | stations:manage | `:110-144` |
| `stations/technical_codes_get` | `station_id` | `{status:{states, public_pin_state, checked_at}, capabilities:{advertised, slots:int[], min, max, locks?:bool}}` | READ (device) | stations:view | `:32-37` → `client/public_codes.py:58-60` |
| `stations/technical_codes_write` | `station_id, slot:int 1..16, action:"add"/"replace"/"remove", door:int (API id in enabled_doors), expected:bool, old_pin:str, new_pin:str, compatibility:bool, confirmed:bool (must be true)` | `{status, capabilities, acknowledged:true, physical_verified:false}` | CONFIG-WRITE device; grants/revokes physical access | stations:manage | `:32-37` → `client/public_codes.py:63-139` |
| `stations/technical_program_list` | `station_id` | `{programs:[program minus identity], saved:[hold_open_drafts for runtime locks], timezone:<HA tz>, native_supported:false}` | READ (storage) | stations:view | `:42-53` |
| `stations/technical_program_save` | `station_id, door:int (physical_index of a runtime lock), revision:int (0 new / current), policy:{timezone:str≤64 IANA, schedule:{name, weekly, holidays}}, enabled:bool` | `{programs:[…]}` | enabled=true: PHYSICAL (scheduled); enabled=false: CONFIG-WRITE storage only | stations:manage | `:54-75`, `:80` |
| `stations/technical_program_action` | `station_id, door:int, revision:int, action:"pause"/"remove"` | `{programs:[…]}` | PHYSICAL (immediate `close` if owned) + CONFIG-WRITE storage | stations:manage | `:76-80` → `hold_programs.py:156-173` |
| `stations/technical_hold_get` | `station_id, door:int (physical_index in runtime locks)` | `{draft:null or {station_id, door, revision, policy}, active:false, blocker:"schedule_writes_unverified", timezone}` | READ (storage) | stations:view | `:81-109` |
| `stations/technical_hold_save` | `station_id, door, revision:int (0 new / current), policy:{timezone, schedule}` | same shape with saved draft | CONFIG-WRITE storage only | stations:manage | `:98-101` |
| `stations/technical_hold_delete` | `station_id, door, revision:int (must equal current)` | `{deleted:true}` | CONFIG-WRITE storage only | stations:manage | `:95-97` |

**Program save details** (`:54-75`): lock must exist with `physical_index == door` else `operation_unsupported`; if `enabled`: `client.async_confirm_identity()` + `verify_hold_support(client, lock.api_id)` (device reads); `programs.update(entry_id, door, revision, policy, runtime.profile.unique_id (identity), lock.api_id, enabled)`; then deletes any legacy hold-open draft for that door.

**Relay details** (`:110-144`): every selected `api_id` must be in `runtime.profile.api_door_ids` else `operation_unsupported`; if a previously managed `(physical, api)` pair is being removed and a hold program exists on that physical door → `hold_pause_before_edit` (note: raised even if the program is paused/inactive); if removed and `manager.has_access(entry_id)` (any bindings / active assigned users / pending tombstones) → `access_removal_pending`. Writes `entry.data.locks` (with `confirmed:true`), schedules `async_reload`.

**Persistence**: via `hold_open_drafts`, `hold_programs` (below) and HA config entry data (`locks`).

**Device interaction**: see `client/technical.py`, `client/public_codes.py`. Direct reads here: `GET /ISAPI/AccessControl/capabilities`, `GET /ISAPI/VideoIntercom/capabilities`, `GET /ISAPI/VideoIntercom/PrivilegePasswordStatus` (`:161-191`).

**Errors raised**: `station_unloaded`, `device_busy`, `operation_unsupported`, `invalid_fields`, `invalid_storage`, `revision_conflict`, `hold_pause_before_edit`, `access_removal_pending`, plus those of called modules; Hikvision errors → `device_unavailable`.

## Module: `client/technical.py`

**Responsibility**: Allowlisted DoorParam read/write, privilege-password status projection, and the hold-open ISAPI adapter.

- `FIELDS = ("doorName","openDuration","relayReverseEnabled")`; `PASSWORD_FIELDS` = engineeringConfigured, setupAlarmConfigured, householderUnlockConfigured, antiHijackingConfigured, public1Configured…public16Configured, sendCardConfigured (`:17-25`).
- `read_door(client, door)` (`:86-96`): door ∈ {1,2}; `GET /ISAPI/AccessControl/Door/param/{door}/capabilities` (root `DoorParam`) → `constraints`: doorName/openDuration `{type:"text"/"integer", min, max}` from `@min/@max` (max ≤64 for name, ≤255 for duration, else error); relayReverseEnabled `{type:"boolean"}` if `@opt` is `true,false`; `GET /ISAPI/AccessControl/Door/param/{door}` → values. Returns only constraints for present values.
- `update_door` (`:99-144`): changes must be non-empty subset of FIELDS; under `asyncio.timeout(40)` and `client._write_lock`: confirm identity, fresh `read_door`; `expected != current.values` → `HikvisionValidationError` ("Door parameters changed; reload before saving" → WS `device_unavailable`); each change validated against advertised constraint (bool / int in range / string length in range without control chars); if desired differs, **PUT `/ISAPI/AccessControl/Door/param/{door}`** XML `<DoorParam xmlns="http://www.isapi.org/ver20/XMLSchema" version="2.0">` with only changed nodes (bools lowercase); readback must equal desired else "Technical change not confirmed by readback". No retry.
- `password_status(payload)` (`:147-159`): booleans per field; `public_pin_state` = configured if any public true, absent if all false, else unknown.
- `hold_command(client, door, command, *, commissioned=False)` (`:162-188`): requires `commissioned` (else `schedule_writes_unverified`); `door ∈ client.enabled_doors` (API ids) and command ∈ {`alwaysOpen`,`close`} else `operation_unsupported`; under `asyncio.timeout(30)` + `client._write_lock`: confirm identity, `verify_hold_support`, **PUT `/ISAPI/AccessControl/RemoteControl/door/{door}`** body `<RemoteControlDoor version="2.0" xmlns="http://www.isapi.org/ver20/XMLSchema"><cmd>{alwaysOpen|close}</cmd></RemoteControlDoor>`; every `statusCode` in response must be "1" else `ambiguous_write`. **PHYSICAL.**
- `verify_hold_support(client, door)` (`:191-203`): `GET /ISAPI/AccessControl/RemoteControl/door/capabilities`; requires `doorNo` bounds contain door and `cmd@opt` ⊇ {alwaysOpen, close} else `operation_unsupported`.
- Doc citation: STATION_MANAGEMENT_AND_SCHEDULING_HE.md:18 — station advertises `open, close, alwaysOpen, resume`; adapter uses only `alwaysOpen`/`close`; `resume` semantics not assumed.

---

## Module: `client/public_codes.py`

**Responsibility**: Public PIN slot management per the station web client contract. Codes are transient, never listed/persisted.

- `BASE = "/ISAPI/VideoIntercom/"`; `TYPES = (5, 6, 7, 9, 10, …, 21)` — slot n → `passwordType = TYPES[n-1]` (slot1=5, slot2=6, slot3=7, slot4=9 … slot16=21; type 8 skipped) (`:18-19`; doc HA_PROGRAMS_PUBLIC_CODES_HE.md:30).
- `status(client)` (`:22-26`): `GET PrivilegePasswordStatus` → `password_status` + `checked_at`.
- `capabilities(client)` (`:37-55`): `GET PrivilegePasswordCfg/capabilities?format=json`; `HikvisionUnsupportedError` → `{advertised:false, slots:[1..16], min:4, max:6}`; else `{advertised:true, slots:[n for which TYPES[n-1] in passwordType@opt], min:max(4,newPassword@min), max:min(16,newPassword@max), locks:"lockIDList" in cap}`; malformed → `invalid_response`.
- `inspect` (`:58-60`): confirm identity + status + capabilities.
- `mutate(client, msg)` (`:63-139`):
  1. slot int 1..16, action ∈ {add, replace, remove} else `invalid_fields`; `confirmed is True` and `expected` bool else `invalid_fields`; door ∈ `client.enabled_doors` else `unmanaged_lock`.
  2. Under `asyncio.timeout(45)` + `client._write_lock`: confirm identity; caps; not advertised and `compatibility is not True` → `operation_unsupported`; slot not in caps.slots → `operation_unsupported`.
  3. Fresh status: `states["public{slot}Configured"] is not expected` → `revision_conflict`; also `expected != (action != "add")` → `revision_conflict` (add requires expected false; replace/remove require true).
  4. `old_pin` (replace/remove): ASCII digits, length 4..16 else `invalid_fields`. `new_pin` (add/replace): ASCII digits, length caps.min..caps.max else `invalid_fields`.
  5. remove: **POST `/ISAPI/VideoIntercom/DeletePrivilegePasswordList?format=json`** body `{"passwordTypeList":[type], "password":"<old>"}`. add/replace: if advertised and caps lacks `locks` → `operation_unsupported`; **PUT `/ISAPI/VideoIntercom/PrivilegePasswordCfg?format=json`** body `{"PrivilegePasswordCfg":{"passwordType":type, "newPassword":"<new>", "lockIDList":[int(door==1), int(door==2)], "oldPassword":"<old>" (replace only)}}` (`application/json`).
  6. `check_response_status`; all `statusCode` must be "1" else `ambiguous_write`; readback status must show slot configured (add/replace) / not configured (remove) else `readback_mismatch`.
- Output `{status, capabilities, acknowledged:true, physical_verified:false}`. No automatic retry.

## Module: `access/hold_open.py`

**Responsibility**: Hold-open policy validation, window token computation, legacy draft storage (`HoldOpenDrafts`) and the durable per-door transition executor (`HoldOpenExecutor`).

- `policy(value)` (`:21-29`): exactly keys `{timezone, schedule}` else `invalid_fields`; `timezone` = `text_field(≤64)` valid `ZoneInfo` else `invalid_timezone`; `schedule` = `schedules.normalize` (see schedules module).
- `window(value, now)` (`:32-43`): tz-aware `now` required (`invalid_time`); converts to policy timezone; uses `schedules.preview(schedule, local date, local HH:MM)` (holiday overrides weekly for that date); returns token `"YYYY-MM-DD/start/end"` of the period containing the time (string compare `start <= HH:MM < end`), else `None`. One token per local date+period (repeated DST hour can't trigger twice).
- **Persistence `.storage/hikvision_intercom.hold_open_drafts`** (`:49-139`): `{"schema":1, "drafts":{"<station_id>/<door>": {"station_id", "door":1/2, "revision":int≥1, "policy":{timezone, schedule}}}}`; ≤200 drafts; key must equal `station/door`, station must not contain "/". `update(station, door, revision, value)`: revision must equal current (0 when absent) else `revision_conflict`; >200 → `schedule_limit`; stores revision+1. `remove`: revision must match else `revision_conflict`.
- `HoldOpenExecutor` (`:142-208`): state `{owned:bool, attempted:str|null (window token ≤128), status: idle/opening/held_acknowledged/restoring/unknown}`; `load` sets `recovering = owned`. `tick(desired_window)` (requires `commissioned` else `schedule_writes_unverified`), under lock:
  - If `owned` and (`recovering` or desired ≠ attempted or status ≠ held_acknowledged): persist `restoring` → `send("close")` (failure → persist `unknown`, re-raise) → persist `owned:false, status:idle`; clear recovering; return. (`attempted` is kept.)
  - Else if desired is None, or owned, or desired == attempted: nothing.
  - Else: persist `owned:true, attempted:desired, status:opening` (intent saved BEFORE I/O) → `send("alwaysOpen")` (failure → `unknown`, re-raise) → persist `held_acknowledged`.
- Runtime semantics (derived): an unknown/failed open is followed by a `close` on the next tick and is **not** re-opened in the same window; after HA restart with `owned:true` the first tick sends `close`, and the door is not re-opened until the next window (attempted token unchanged). A window boundary between two back-to-back windows (e.g. 00:00–24:00 on consecutive days → token changes at midnight) produces `close` then, one tick later (≈15 s), `alwaysOpen`.

---

## Module: `access/hold_programs.py`

**Responsibility**: Persistent HA hold-open programs (one per station/door) and their periodic execution.

- **Persistence `.storage/hikvision_intercom.hold_programs`** (`:23-75`): `{"schema":1, "programs":{"<station_id>/<door>": {"station_id", "door":1/2 (physical), "api_id":1/2, "identity":str (runtime.profile.unique_id, ≤512), "revision":int≥1, "policy":{timezone, schedule}, "enabled":bool, "removing":bool, "execution":{owned, attempted, status}, "error":null/"technical_write_unknown", "checked_at":null/ISO}}}`; ≤200.
- `listing(station)` (`:77-82`): all programs of the station minus `identity`.
- `update(station, door, revision, value, identity, api_id, enabled)` (`:118-154`): revision must equal current (0 when new) else `revision_conflict`; if existing program is `enabled` or `execution.owned` or `removing` → `hold_pause_before_edit`; >200 → `schedule_limit`; writes a fresh record (revision+1, execution reset to `{owned:false, attempted:null, status:"idle"}`, error null, checked_at null) and drops the cached worker. **No immediate tick** — the next 15-s timer tick acts.
- `action(station, door, revision, action)` (`:156-173`): action ∈ {pause, remove} else `invalid_fields`; revision must match; persists `enabled:false, removing:(action=="remove"), revision+1`; then **immediately** `tick_key(key, now)` → sends `close` if the executor owns the door.
- `tick_key(key, now)` (`:175-198`): desired = `window(policy, now)` if enabled and not removing else None; `worker.tick(desired)`; any exception → persist `error:"technical_write_unknown"` and return; if `removing` and not owned → delete record + worker; else clear error. Worker `save` persists `execution` + `checked_at = utc_now()`; worker `send(command)` → `send_hold(program, command)`.
- `tick(now)` (`:200-207`): all programs concurrently with Semaphore(3).
- **Runtime wiring** (`access_runtime.py:156-183`): `send_hold(item, command)` requires loaded runtime whose `profile.unique_id == item.identity` (else `station_unloaded`) and a runtime lock with `physical_index == door` and `api_id == item.api_id` (else `operation_unsupported`), then `hold_command(runtime.client, item.api_id, command, commissioned=True)`. `async_track_time_interval(hass, tick_programs, 15 s)`; overlapping ticks skipped via `program_tick_lock`; timer cancelled on HA stop.
- **Net physical behaviour**: for every enabled program, every ~15 s HA evaluates the window in the program's timezone; entering a window → one `PUT RemoteControl/door/{api_id}` `alwaysOpen` (door kept unlocked); leaving the window, pause, remove, identity/lock-mapping problems, or HA restart while owned → `close`. If HA/network is down at window end the door stays held open (HA_PROGRAMS_PUBLIC_CODES_HE.md:16; i18n `hold_dependency`).

---

## Module: `access/schedules.py`

**Responsibility**: Central schedule drafts (library) — validation, preview evaluation, import/export. "No device allocation, assignment, or write is performed." (`:1`)

- Constants: `DAYS = Monday..Sunday`, `MAX_SCHEDULES=100`, `MAX_HOLIDAYS=64`, `TRANSFER_FORMAT="hikvision_intercom.schedule_drafts"`, `MAX_TRANSFER_BYTES=8 MiB` (`:19-23`).
- `normalize(data)` (`:97-126`): keys exactly `{name, weekly, holidays}` else `invalid_fields`; `name` = text ≤32 non-blank, no control chars, stripped (`invalid_text`); `weekly` keys exactly the 7 DAYS else `schedule_invalid_week`; each day `periods()`; `holidays` list ≤64 else `schedule_holiday_limit`; each holiday keys exactly `{name,start,end,periods}` (`invalid_fields`), dates `YYYY-MM-DD` valid, year 2000..2037 (`schedule_invalid_date`), start ≤ end; sorted by start; holiday ranges must not overlap (`a.end >= b.start` → `schedule_holiday_overlap`).
- `periods(value)` (`:65-82`): list ≤8 (`schedule_period_limit`); each `{start,end}` exactly; `start` `HH:MM` 00:00–23:59, `end` same or `"24:00"` (`schedule_invalid_time`); start < end; sorted; overlap (`prev.end > next.start`) → `schedule_overlap` (touching allowed).
- `preview(data, on_date, at_time)` (`:129-147`): → `{date, time, weekday, source:"holiday"/"weekly", holiday:name/null, periods, within_window: [start,end), basis:"draft_local_time", applied:false}`.
- **Persistence `.storage/hikvision_intercom.schedules`** (`:159-194`): `{"schema":1, "schedules":{"<uuid>": {"id", "revision":int≥1, "updated_at":tz-aware ISO, "name", "weekly", "holidays"}}}`; ≤100. Missing file → saved empty.
- Commands (dispatch inline `websocket.py:612-632`):

| Command | Input | Output | Classification | Permission | file:line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schedules/list` | — | Schedule[] sorted by (name casefold, id) | READ | management:view | `schedules.py:196-200` |
| `schedules/create` | `data:{name,weekly,holidays}` | Schedule (revision 1, new uuid4) | CONFIG-WRITE storage | management:manage | `:215-235` |
| `schedules/update` | `schedule_id:uuid, revision:int, data` | Schedule (revision+1) | CONFIG-WRITE storage | management:manage | `:215-235`, `_require :311-317` |
| `schedules/delete` | `schedule_id, revision` | `{deleted:true}` | CONFIG-WRITE storage | management:manage | `:319-324` |
| `schedules/preview` | `data, date:"YYYY-MM-DD", time:"HH:MM"` | preview dict | READ (pure) | management:manage | `:129-147` |
| `schedules/export` | — | `{format, version:1, schedules:[{name,weekly,holidays}]}` | READ | management:view | `:237-244` |
| `schedules/import_preview` | `document:str` (JSON text) | `{token, count, name_collisions, expires_in:300, mode:"append", items:[{name, weekly_periods, holidays}]}` | READ (in-memory pending; per-actor single pending, ≤16 total, 300 s) | management:manage | `:249-288` |
| `schedules/import_apply` | `token:str` | Schedule[] (new uuids, revision 1) | CONFIG-WRITE storage | management:manage | `:290-309` |

- Import document (`transfer_document`, `:26-53`): keys exactly `{format, version, schedules}`, format constant, version int 1, 1..100 schedules, each `normalize`d; duplicate JSON keys rejected; any failure → `schedule_transfer_invalid`. Apply: token must exist, same actor, unexpired (`schedule_import_expired`); library versions snapshot must be unchanged since preview (`revision_conflict`); total >100 → `schedule_limit`.
- Every successful mutation calls `changed()` → WS subscribe `refresh`.
- Errors: `invalid_fields`, `invalid_text`, `invalid_id`, `schedule_invalid_week`, `schedule_period_limit`, `schedule_invalid_time`, `schedule_overlap`, `schedule_invalid_date`, `schedule_holiday_limit`, `schedule_holiday_overlap`, `schedule_limit`, `schedule_not_found`, `revision_conflict`, `schedule_transfer_invalid`, `schedule_import_expired`, `invalid_storage` (library unavailable).

## Module: `access/schedule_assessment.py`

**Responsibility**: Compare one draft to advertised device limits from an inventory, no allocation/writes (`assess(draft, inventory)`, `:10-95`).
- `requirements = {template:1, weekly:1, holiday_group: 1 if holidays else 0, holiday: len(holidays), weekly_periods: total weekly periods}`.
- `limits[]` entries `{key, needed, available (null=unknown), state: "unknown"/"fits"/"exceeds"}` with keys: `template_resources`, `weekly_resources`, `holiday_group_resources`, `holiday_resources` (available = ids range size), `weekly_per_day`, `weekly_periods` (vs `max_periods`), `weekly_precision` (count of non-hour-aligned times if device precision is "hour"), `holiday_per_day`, `holiday_periods`, `holiday_precision`, `weekdays` (days with windows not in advertised weekdays), `holiday_membership` (always available=null → unknown).
- Output `{requirements, limits, state: exceeds/unknown/fits, can_apply:false, inventory_complete, blockers:["schedule_writes_unverified","schedule_ownership_unknown"] + ["schedule_inventory_incomplete" if incomplete]}`.
- Used by `schedules/assess` (`websocket.py:586-587`). READ.

## Module: `access/schedule_baselines.py`

**Responsibility**: Private HMAC fingerprints of observed schedule records per station and explicit, revision-checked "comparison baselines". "A baseline records observations, never ownership or permission to mutate the station." (`:3`)
- **Persistence `.storage/hikvision_intercom.schedule_baselines`** (`:115-147`): `{"schema":1, "key":<64-hex HMAC key>, "stations":{"<station_id ≤64>": {"revision":1..2^31-1, "checked_at":ISO, "identity":<64-hex>, "snapshot":{template|weekly|holiday_group|holiday: {"state": complete/partial/failed/unsupported/not_checked, "total":int|null ≤4096, "rows":{"<id>":<64-hex>}, "capability":<64-hex>|null}}}}}`; ≤16 stations.
- `fingerprint(value)` = HMAC-SHA256(key, canonical JSON).
- `observe(station, actor, identity, checked_at, snapshot)` (`:165-199`): result `{revision, checked_at, state:"missing", checks:[], token:null}`; if baseline exists: same identity → `compare(old, new)` (state `changed`/`unchanged`/`incomplete` with per-kind `{kind, state, modified, added, removed, modified_ids[≤20], added_ids[≤20], removed_ids[≤20], unverified_new, unverified_missing, coverage_complete, capability_changed}`), else `{state:"identity_changed", checks:[]}`. Issues an in-memory save token (uuid4, 300 s, one per station, ≤16) when actor set and some kind complete/partial.
- `async_save(station, actor, identity, token)` (`:214-242`): token must match station/actor/identity/unexpired (`schedule_baseline_expired`); revision must still match (`revision_conflict`); station cap 16 / revision overflow → `schedule_baseline_limit`; stores snapshot, revision+1 → returns `{revision, checked_at}`.
- `async_clear(station, revision)` (`:244-251`): revision must equal current (`revision_conflict`) → removes → `{revision:0, checked_at:null}`.
- Commands (`websocket.py:545-558`): `schedules/baseline_save {station_id, token}` and `schedules/baseline_clear {station_id, revision}` — CONFIG-WRITE storage only; management:manage. Save computes identity = `baselines.fingerprint([driver.client._expected_identity, runtime.profile.firmware])` (station must be registered + driver present → `station_not_found`/`station_offline`/`station_has_no_managed_lock`). Unavailable store → `schedule_baseline_unavailable`.
- When assess cannot produce evidence, baseline is `{state:"unavailable", revision:0, checked_at:null, token:null, checks:[]}` (`websocket.py:588-594`).

---

## Module: `access/schedule_comparison.py`

**Responsibility**: Strict canonical projection of observed native schedule records and field comparison (`canonical(kind, value)`, `compare_resource(kind, desired, observed)`).
- `ID_KEYS`: template `planTemplateID`, weekly `weekPlanID`, holiday_group `holidayGroupID`, holiday `holidayPlanID` (`:12-17`).
- `canonical` (`:20-117`): unwraps root (`ROOTS[kind]`), requires bool `enable`; template: `templateName` (≤64), `holidayGroupNo` (comma string → sorted unique ints 1..65535), `weekPlanNo` int; holiday_group: `groupName`, `holidayPlanNo` (+ allowed GET-only `holidayPlanName`); weekly: `WeekPlanCfg` rows ≤56 `{week, id 1..8, enable, TimeSegment{beginTime,endTime "HH:MM:SS" / "24:00:00"}}`; holiday: `beginDate`/`endDate` (may be `0000-00-00` when disabled), `HolidayPlanCfg` ≤8 rows, allowed `holidayPlanName`. Unknown fields → `schedule_observation_extra_fields`; other defects → `schedule_observation_invalid`.
- `compare_resource` (`:120-138`) → `{state: not_observed/unsupported/unreadable/different/matches, fields:[differing keys], active: observed enable or null}`.

## Module: `access/schedule_compiler.py`

**Responsibility**: Compile a draft + explicit ID bindings + device capabilities into candidate ISAPI bodies. "Contains no network writer." (`:1`)
- `ROOTS = {template:"UserRightPlanTemplate", weekly:"UserRightWeekPlanCfg", holiday_group:"UserRightHolidayGroupCfg", holiday:"UserRightHolidayPlanCfg"}` (`:13-18`).
- `bindings_for(data, holiday_count)` (`:21-41`): keys exactly `{template, weekly, holiday_group, holidays}`; `holidays` list length == draft holiday count; `holiday_group` required int iff holidays exist else must be null; all ids int 1..65535; holiday ids unique → else `schedule_binding_invalid`.
- `compile_schedule(draft, bindings, caps)` (`:44-181`) → list of `{key:"kind:id", kind, id, dependencies:[keys], body:{ROOT:{…}}}` in order: weekly (`{enable:true, WeekPlanCfg:[{week, id, enable, TimeSegment{beginTime "HH:MM:00", endTime}}]}` — fills ALL period ids per weekday, unused ones `enable:false 00:00:00`), each holiday (`{enable:true, beginDate, endDate, HolidayPlanCfg}`), holiday_group if holidays (`{enable:true, groupName:<draft name>, holidayPlanNo:"id,id"}`), template (`{enable:true, templateName:<draft name>, weekPlanNo, holidayGroupNo:"<gid>" or ""}`). Errors: `schedule_compilation_unknown` (missing/invalid capability), `schedule_binding_out_of_range`, `schedule_compilation_limit` (too many periods / hour precision misalignment / max_periods).

---

## Module: `access/schedule_executor.py`

**Responsibility**: Readback-driven executor over a `ScheduleJournal`, usable only with a transport whose `writes_verified is True`.
- `ScheduleObservation(context:dict[str,str], records:dict, eligible:bool)`; `ScheduleTransport` protocol: `writes_verified`, `observe(transaction)`, `write(resource)` (`:21-40`).
- `_observe` (`:51-87`): observe with timeout (≤60 s), validate context, records keys == compiled keys, HMAC each canonical record; failures → journal `issue="read_failed"`; `eligible` false or context changed → `issue="context_changed"`; any step hash not in accepted set → `issue="resource_changed"`.
- `recover(id)` (`:108-113`): read-only; never resends an intent; marks intent step verified if observed == after, else `write_uncertain`.
- `execute(id)` (`:115-166`): requires `transport.writes_verified` else `schedule_writes_unverified`; for each compiled resource in order: skip verified; observe; if before==after → verified; else record `intent` (persisted BEFORE I/O), re-observe; if already after → verified; else `transport.write(resource)` then recover; stop on failure/conflict.
- **In Part E's public API the executor is only used via `recover()` with `ReadOnlySnapshot` (writes_verified False)** (`schedule_operations_api.py:22-34,146-148`). `execute()` is called by `access/native_timing.py:95` (user timing enforcement, outside Part E) with `_LockedTransport(writes_verified=True)`, which does write native schedules to the device.

## Module: `access/schedule_journal.py`

**Responsibility**: Private write-ahead journal for native schedule transactions ("Save intent before I/O; never discard ambiguous or partially applied work", `:43`).
- **Persistence `.storage/hikvision_intercom.schedule_journal`** (`:155-207`): `{"schema":2, "key":<64-hex>, "transactions":{"<uuid>": T}, "archive":[T (verified only), ≤128]}`; schema 1 `{schema,key,transactions}` auto-migrated to 2. ≤1024 transactions; at most one non-verified transaction per station.
- Transaction T (`:62-141`, `:254-277`): `{id:uuid, revision:1..2^31-1, station_id, context:{identity, capability, dependencies, ownership, source (all 64-hex)}, draft, bindings, capabilities, steps:[{key, before:<hash>, after:<hash of compiled body>, state: pending/intent/verified, attempted:bool}], status: ready/recovery_required/conflict/verified, issue: null/read_failed/write_uncertain/context_changed/resource_changed, created_at, updated_at}`. Status derived: conflict if issue ∈ {context_changed, resource_changed}; else recovery_required if any intent; else verified if all verified; else ready.
- `public(id)` → `{id, revision, status, issue, created_at, updated_at, steps:[{key, state, attempted}]}` (`:217-225`); `all()` lists public views of live transactions.
- `async_prepare(...)` (`:227-286`): requires owned == observed keys == compiled keys (`schedule_deployment_ownership_required`), limit (`schedule_deployment_limit`), one open transaction per station (`schedule_deployment_busy`).
- `async_record` (internal only; "no public API is registered", `:308`), `async_discard_unstarted` (all steps pending, not running, else `schedule_deployment_retained`), `async_archive_verified` (verified only), `archived(id)`.
- Errors: `schedule_deployment_not_found`, `revision_conflict`, `schedule_deployment_terminal`, `schedule_deployment_invalid`, `schedule_deployment_busy`, `schedule_deployment_retained`, `schedule_deployment_limit`, `schedule_deployment_ownership_required`, `invalid_storage`.
- Shared instance: also used by `NativeTiming` (`access_runtime.py:265-268`) — its (device-writing) transactions appear in `schedules/operations_list` → `journal`.

## Module: `access/schedule_operations.py`

**Responsibility**: Local resource responsibility claims, deployment jobs and bounded archive. "An administrator declaration records management responsibility, not proof that a resource is unused or permission to bypass device/protocol/dependency checks." (`:3-4`)
- **Persistence `.storage/hikvision_intercom.schedule_operations`** (`:185-240`): `{"schema":1, "key":<64-hex>, "claims":{"<uuid>": Claim} (≤64), "jobs":{"<uuid>": Job} (≤32), "archive":[Job (status verified/cancelled), ≤128]}`. No resource may be claimed twice per station. On load, jobs in `queued`/`checking` become `interrupted` with `error:"schedule_operation_interrupted"`, revision+1.
- Claim (`:102-123`): `{id, revision, plan_id, station_id, identity:<plan identity hash>, members:{"kind:id": <HMAC of canonical observed record>} (1..67), created_at}`; public view `{id, revision, plan_id, station_id, created_at, resource_keys}`.
- Job (`:125-171`): `{id, revision, plan_id, plan_revision, station_id, name (≤64), resource_keys (1..67 unique), created_at, updated_at, status, error, blockers, report (plan report shape or null), journal_id (uuid|null), ownership: not_checked/missing/current/changed}`. `STATES = pending, queued, checking, blocked, ready, interrupted, failed, cancelled, verified`; `WORK_ERRORS = schedule_operation_failed, schedule_source_changed, schedule_plan_not_found, schedule_operation_interrupted, schedule_read_busy, station_offline, station_unloaded, authentication_failed, connection_failed, schedule_ownership_changed, schedule_plan_device_changed` (`:27-50`). Blockers ⊆ `schedule_plans.BLOCKERS ∪ WORK_ERRORS`.
- `ownership(plan, inspection)` (`:264-280`): claims on the station overlapping current members; none → `missing`; all current hashes equal claimed hashes (same plan identity) → `current`; else `changed`.
- `preview_claim` (`:282-321`): overlapping existing claim → `schedule_claim_conflict`; pending token 300 s (per actor, ≤16) → `{token, plan_id, plan_revision, resource_keys, report}`.
- `async_claim` (`:329-351`): `schedule_claim_expired`, `revision_conflict` (plan revision/identity changed), `schedule_operation_limit` (64), `schedule_claim_conflict`.
- `async_release` (`:353-367`): revision match; in use by a non-cancelled/non-verified job → `schedule_claim_in_use`.
- `async_create(plan)` (`:377-411`): ≤32 jobs (`schedule_operation_limit`); one active job per plan (`schedule_operation_exists`); initial `status:"pending", blockers:["schedule_writes_unverified"], ownership:"not_checked"`.
- `async_update` (patch keys ⊆ status/error/blockers/report/journal_id/ownership; not on cancelled/verified → `schedule_operation_invalid`); `async_archive` (only cancelled/verified else `schedule_operation_retained`).

## Module: `access/schedule_plans.py`

**Responsibility**: Durable local deployment proposals and ID reservations, never device ownership or writes (`:1`).
- `BLOCKERS` (`:25-36`): `schedule_writes_unverified`, `schedule_ownership_unknown`, `schedule_inventory_incomplete`, `schedule_plan_users_unreadable`, `schedule_plan_user_defaults`, `schedule_plan_external_references`, `schedule_plan_capabilities_changed`, `schedule_plan_active_resources`, `schedule_plan_observation_incomplete`, `schedule_plan_holiday_membership_unknown`. `FIELDS` (comparable) = enable, templateName, weekPlanNo, holidayGroupNo, groupName, holidayPlanNo, WeekPlanCfg, beginDate, endDate, HolidayPlanCfg.
- Report shape (`validate_report`, `:56-126`): `{checked_at, can_apply:false (must), blockers (⊇ writes_unverified + ownership_unknown), resources:[{kind, id, coverage: complete/partial/failed/unsupported/not_checked, state: matches/different/not_observed/unreadable/unsupported, fields:[FIELDS], active: bool|null, externally_referenced: bool|null}] (one per compiled candidate, same order), users:{state: complete/failed, error: SAFE_ERRORS|null, read, explicit, implicit, malformed (int 0..20000|null)}}`.
- **Persistence `.storage/hikvision_intercom.schedule_plans`** (`:146-227`): `{"schema":1, "key":<64-hex>, "plans":{"<uuid>": {id, revision, station_id, identity:<64-hex>, draft_id:uuid, draft_revision, draft, bindings, capabilities, capability_fingerprint, fingerprints:{"kind:id": <hash>|null}, drifted_resources:["kind:id"], created_at, report}}}`; ≤32 plans; a resource key may be reserved by only one plan per station.
- `public(item, details)` (`:237-257`): `{id, revision, station_id, draft_id, draft_revision, bindings, drifted_resources, created_at, report, name, can_apply:false, candidates?}`.
- `preview(...)` (`:272-312`): builds item, `_reserve` (`schedule_plan_resource_reserved`), ≤32 (`schedule_plan_limit`), in-memory token 300 s per actor ≤16 → `{…public(details), token}`.
- `async_save(token, actor, identity, draft_revision)` (`:332-348`): `schedule_plan_expired`, `schedule_plan_device_changed`, `revision_conflict` (source draft revision changed), reserve/limit checks.
- `async_recheck(id, revision, identity, inspection)` (`:350-380`): revision+1, new report; capability fingerprint/capabilities differ → append `schedule_plan_capabilities_changed`; `drifted_resources` = keys whose fingerprint changed since save.
- `async_delete(id, revision)` (`:382-387`).

## Module: `access/schedule_work_queue.py`

**Responsibility**: Bounded per-station background preflight ("there is no production write queue", `:1`).
- `request(job_id, revision)` (`:32-72`): job revision must match; closed → `station_unloaded`; station already has a task or job queued/checking → `schedule_read_busy`; persist `status:"queued", error:null`; spawn `hass.async_create_background_task(preflight)`; spawn failure → `failed`/`schedule_operation_failed`. Returns queued job. Calls `changed()`.
- `_run` (`:74-106`): Semaphore(3); persist `checking`; `preflight(hass, job)`; persist result patch; exceptions → `status:"failed", error:<code if in WORK_ERRORS else schedule_operation_failed>`.
- `cancel(job_id, revision, cleanup)` (`:108-120`): station task running → `schedule_operation_retained`; cleanup (journal discard); persist `cancelled, error:null, journal_id:null`.
- `close()` on HA stop cancels tasks (`access_runtime.py:273-276`).

- Source schedule looked up in library (`source`, `:19-28`): `invalid_storage`, `schedule_not_found`, `revision_conflict`. Store unavailable → `schedule_plan_storage_unavailable`.

Recheck compiles with the stored capabilities as `expected`.

## Module: `schedule_operations_api.py`

**Responsibility**: HA bridge for claims, jobs, background preflight and read-only journal recovery.

| Command | Input | Output | Classification | Permission | file:line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schedules/operations_list` | — | `{claims, jobs, archive, journal:[journal.public…], writes_enabled:false}` | READ | management:view | `:165-166` |
| `schedules/operations_export` | — | identical to list | READ | management:view | `:165-166` |
| `schedules/operations_claim_preview` | `plan_id, revision` | `{token, plan_id, plan_revision, resource_keys, report}` | READ device | management:manage | `:167-169` |
| `schedules/operations_claim_confirm` | `token` | claim public | CONFIG-WRITE storage | management:manage | `:170-173` |
| `schedules/operations_claim_release` | `claim_id, revision` | `{released:true}` | CONFIG-WRITE storage | management:manage | `:174-176` |
| `schedules/operations_create` | `plan_id, revision` | Job | CONFIG-WRITE storage | management:manage | `:177-179` |
| `schedules/operations_check` | `job_id, revision` | Job (queued) | READ device (background) + CONFIG-WRITE storage | management:manage | `:180-181` |
| `schedules/operations_cancel` | `job_id, revision` | Job (cancelled) | CONFIG-WRITE storage | management:manage | `:182-193` |
| `schedules/operations_archive` | `job_id, revision` | `{archived:true}` | CONFIG-WRITE storage | management:manage | `:194-208` |

- `checked_plan` (`:53-69`): plan revision match; source draft must still exist at the plan's `draft_revision` else `schedule_source_changed`; identity changed → `schedule_plan_device_changed`.
- `read` (`:72-94`): same `schedule_reads` busy set / 130 s / read slots as plan API; `inspect_plan(driver.client, draft, bindings, plans.fingerprint)`.
- `preflight(hass, job)` (`:97-156`): read; blockers = report blockers; ownership via claims (`current` removes `schedule_ownership_unknown`; `changed` adds `schedule_ownership_changed`); capability fingerprint change adds `schedule_plan_capabilities_changed`. If the only remaining blocker is `schedule_writes_unverified`: builds context `{identity, capability, ownership, dependencies, source}` and either prepares a new journal transaction (id = job id) or runs read-only `ScheduleExecutor(journal, ReadOnlySnapshot).recover(journal_id)`. **Always returns `status:"blocked"`** with `{error:null, blockers, report, journal_id, ownership}` — `ready`/`verified` are never produced by this API.
- `ReadOnlySnapshot.writes_verified = False`; `write()` raises `schedule_writes_unverified` (`:22-34`).
- Cancel cleanup: discards the journal transaction if all steps pending (else `schedule_deployment_retained`).
- Archive: if job has `journal_id`, archives the verified journal transaction (or accepts already-archived).
- Unavailable stores → `schedule_operations_unavailable`.

## Module: `client/schedule_inventory.py`

**Responsibility**: Paged read-only inventory of the four native schedule families via POST Search. "POST /Search is a read operation. Disabled records are never considered free slots." (`:3`)
- Uses a separate `HikvisionClient` reader sharing session/settings/expected identity, isolated from the call/release I/O lock (`:193-195`); `asyncio.timeout(60)`.
- Device reads: `GET /ISAPI/AccessControl/capabilities` (requires both family flag and `isSupportSearchUserRight{PlanTemplate|WeekPlan|HolidayGroup|HolidayPlan}`); `GET /ISAPI/AccessControl/{root}/capabilities?format=json` (weekly also requires `WeekPlanCfg.week@opt` weekdays); `GET /ISAPI/AccessControl/{root}/Search/capabilities?format=json` (searchID range must include 32, position min 0/1, page size ≤50, `enable@opt` includes false); up to 32 × **POST `/ISAPI/AccessControl/{root}/Search?format=json`** `{"searchID":<uuid hex>, "searchResultPosition":n, "maxResults":≤50, "enable":false}` with strict paging consistency checks.
- Output (`:340-347`): `{checked_at, checks:[{kind, state: not_checked/unsupported/complete/partial/failed, error, capabilities, search:{start,last_start,page_size}, read, total, pages, enabled, disabled, referenced}], complete, can_apply:false, ownership_checked:false, users_checked:false}`; optional out-params `records` (selected raw rows), `projected` (id/enabled/references/week), `evidence` (per-kind `{state,total,rows:{id:hmac},capability:hmac}` for baselines).
- Errors per kind: `operation_unsupported`, `schedule_inventory_invalid`, `schedule_search_bound`, device error codes; auth/connection/timeout abort the whole read.

## Module: `client/schedule_dependencies.py`

**Responsibility**: Read-only anonymous dependency audit of user `RightPlan` references (`inspect_dependencies`, `read_user_dependencies`, `summarize`).
- Reads schedule inventory, then all users via `AccessClient(reader)._search("UserInfo")` (60 s) — UserInfo Search on the device; per user `RightPlan:[{doorNo 1..128, planTemplateNo:"1,2"}]`; empty/missing = implicit (unknown defaults); malformed counted separately (`:16-58`).
- Output (`:61-115`): `{checked_at, users_checked, mapping_complete, can_apply:false, ownership_checked:false, users:{state, error, read, explicit, implicit, malformed}, checks:[{kind, coverage, referenced, observed, not_observed, disabled, ids[≤20], not_observed_ids[≤20]}]}`; counts nulled when users unread.
- Command `schedules/dependencies {station_id}`: READ (device), management:view, 130 s timeout, busy set `schedule_reads` (`websocket.py:559-611`). Doc: SCHEDULE_WORKFLOWS.md:3-20.

## Module: `client/schedule_plan_inspection.py`

**Responsibility**: `inspect_plan(client, draft, bindings, fingerprint, *, expected=None, ignore_employee=None)` (`:18-136`): inventory with selected IDs, compile candidates (or use `expected`), user dependency read, per-candidate comparison, blockers. Returns private `{external_context, observed:{key: raw record|null}, dependency_fingerprint, capability_fingerprint, capabilities, fingerprints:{key: hmac|null}, candidates, report}`. Blockers: always `schedule_writes_unverified`, `schedule_ownership_unknown`; plus `schedule_inventory_incomplete`, `schedule_plan_users_unreadable` / `schedule_plan_user_defaults`, `schedule_plan_external_references`, `schedule_plan_active_resources` (any observed target enabled), `schedule_plan_observation_incomplete`, `schedule_plan_holiday_membership_unknown` (any holidays). READ only.

## Module: `client/schedule_transport.py`

**Responsibility**: `CommissioningScheduleTransport` — a journal-bound transport that can **PUT `/ISAPI/AccessControl/{ROOT}/{id}?format=json`** with the compiled body (inside `driver.transaction()`, requires `_require_mutation("UserInfo","put")`, only for the current intent step, once, after a fresh eligible observation matching the BEFORE image; all statusCodes must be "1") (`:26-94`). `writes_verified = authorized is True`. **Not referenced by any production module** (only `tests/test_schedule_transport.py`). NO SCREEN / not reachable via WS.

## Module: `access/permission_audit.py`

**Responsibility**: `inspect_permissions(manager, station_id)` (`:17-90`): read-only comparison of retained desired users with a complete station inventory.
- Under `asyncio.timeout(90)`, `manager._read_slots`, `driver.transaction()` (station I/O lock): confirm identity, `driver.async_capabilities()`, `driver.async_inventory()` (device reads of full user/card inventory). Repository `bulk_stamp` must be unchanged before and after (else `review_stale`).
- Rows for users assigned to or bound to the station (≤1000): `{user_id, display_name, employee_no, revision, differences:[presence, display_name, user_type, validity, door_rights, pin, schedule, privileged, other_credentials, cards], plan:{person: create/delete/update/none, pin: none/remove/set/change, cards_add, cards_remove, cards_update}, error, status: matched/drift/unmanaged/unverified}`; plus unmanaged station employees `{user_id:null, employee_no, display_name:null, revision:null, status:"unmanaged", differences:[], error:null}`.
- Output `{station_id, checked_at, device_writes:0, complete, rows, counts:{matched, drift, unmanaged, unverified}, total_candidates}`.
- Dispatch `admin_operations_api.py:69-80`: busy set `permission_audits` (same station or ≥3 → `device_busy`), `TimeoutError` → `permission_timeout`; no actor → `unauthorized`. Permission stations:view. READ.

## Open questions

1. `schedules/import_preview` accepts documents up to 8 MiB server-side (`schedules.py:23,38`) and the UI allows files ≤ 8 MiB (`schedules.ts:491`), but the WS handler rejects any message > 65 536 bytes (`websocket.py:1040-1046`) → `request_too_large`. Effective import limit is ~64 KiB. Intended?
2. `stations/technical_relays` raises `hold_pause_before_edit` when a removed relay's physical door has any hold program, even a paused/inactive one (`technical_api.py:120-125`), so the user must *remove* the program, not pause it, despite the error text.
3. `technical_program_save` with `enabled:true` does not tick immediately (`hold_programs.py:154`); first `alwaysOpen` happens on the next 15-s timer tick. `action` does tick immediately. UI copy does not mention the delay.
4. After HA restart while a program owns the door, recovery sends `close` and, because `attempted` is preserved, the door is not re-held for the rest of that window (`hold_open.py:182-201`). Similarly after an unknown open outcome. Whether this is the intended product behaviour (vs. resuming the hold) is not documented beyond "Lost open responses never trigger a blind repeat within the same window" (`hold_open.py:147`).
5. Back-to-back windows (e.g. 00:00–24:00 on consecutive days, or 08:00–12:00 then 12:00–17:00) change the window token and cause a `close` then `alwaysOpen` ≈15 s later. Unclear if intentional.
6. `hikvision-hold-open` (`hold-open.ts`) is defined and imported but never rendered; `technical_hold_get/save` have no reachable UI. Is it deprecated?
7. Door-programs editor timezone is a free-text field (validated server-side as IANA); no picker. Holiday name always "Date".
8. `schedules/preview` (a pure computation) requires `management:manage` while `schedules/list` needs only `view` — a view-only user cannot evaluate a draft.
9. `technical_api` timeouts (`asyncio.timeout(75)`) and `HikvisionValidationError` (e.g. door params changed since read, relay mapping invalid) surface as generic `action_failed` / `device_unavailable` codes, not specific ones; the UI shows `technical_write_unknown` for all write failures in station-technical.
10. Schedule operations: jobs can never reach `ready`/`verified` through the WS API (preflight always returns `blocked`, `writes_enabled:false`); `verified`/archive-of-verified paths only apply to journal transactions produced by NativeTiming. Confirm that the SMPLWISE tab should present this as read-only/blocked.
11. `STATION_MANAGEMENT_AND_SCHEDULING_HE.md:9,28` (15.09.2026) says hold-open is "not connected to a production timer" and public-code writes are "unavailable"; current code does both (15-s timer at `access_runtime.py:183`; writes in `public_codes.py`). HA_PROGRAMS_PUBLIC_CODES_HE.md (RC10) matches the code. The older doc is stale.
12. `public-codes.ts` editor sends `door` for `remove` too; backend requires it to be a managed API door even though delete ignores it (`public_codes.py:69-71,100-102`). If the station has no managed lock, removal is impossible.

## Common WS envelope facts (apply to every command below)

- Handler factory `websocket.py:989-1076`. Order: (1) authorization via `command_allowed(panel_permissions, user, command)`
  (`panel_permissions.py:329-340`; HA admins always allowed; non-admins need an area/level grant from
  `requirements()` `panel_permissions.py:289-314`) → error `unauthorized`; (2) voluptuous schema — only the
  fields in `COMMANDS` plus `id`, `type`, optional `api_contract:int`; extra keys are rejected (`invalid_fields`).
  Extra optional keys per command: `column_map:dict` for `users/csv_preview|csv_apply`; `sync_now:bool=True`
  for `users/create|update`; `user_id:str`, `revision:int` for `users/adopt` ONLY (`websocket.py:994-1011`);
  (3) `api_contract` must be int in `[0, 1]` else `api_incompatible` (`api_contract.py:5-6,87-91`);
  (4) `int`/`bool` fields type-checked exactly → `invalid_fields`; (5) message size ≤ 65 536 bytes
  (1 048 576 for CSV commands) else `request_too_large`; (6) per-HA-user rate limiter: burst 30, 2/s sustained,
  ≤ 8 concurrent, ≤ 128 tracked users → `rate_limited` (`hardening.py:48-68`).
- Error mapping (`websocket.py:1049-1074`): `AccessError(code)` → WS error code = `code` (translation key
  `access_action_failed`, placeholder `reason`); any `HikvisionError` escaping → `device_unavailable`;
  other exceptions → `action_failed`; `vol.Invalid` → `invalid_fields`. Unknown command → `unknown_command`.
- Commands that return nothing return `{"accepted": True}` (`websocket.py:986`).
- `subscribe` (`websocket.py:1078-1126`): `{"type":"hikvision_intercom/subscribe","id":N}` (no other keys).
  Requires `overview` permission. On `SIGNAL_ACCESS_CHANGED` it coalesces (0.25 s) and sends event
  `{"kind":"refresh"}`; if the user lost permission it sends `{"kind":"access_revoked"}` and unsubscribes.
  No data payload ever.

---

## Module: access_runtime.py

**Responsibility.** One-time (per HA process) construction of all central stores, the `AccessRepository`,
`AccessManager`, schedule queue, hold-program timer, and registration of 4 admin services. Defines the
change signal.

**Key definitions.**
- `SIGNAL_ACCESS_CHANGED = f"{DOMAIN}_access_changed"` → `"hikvision_intercom_access_changed"` (`:29`).
- `get_manager(hass) -> hass.data["hikvision_intercom"]["access"]` (`:32-33`).
- `async_setup_access(hass)` (`:36-279`) called from `__init__.py:37` in `async_setup` (not per entry).
  - `changed()` callback (`:48-51`) = `async_dispatcher_send(hass, SIGNAL_ACCESS_CHANGED)`; "carries no personal data".
  - Constructs, in order, every `AccessStore` (see Storage boundary) and puts objects into `hass.data[DOMAIN]`
    under keys: `panel_permissions`, `appearance_settings`, `media_settings`, `whatsapp_templates`, `ntp_settings`,
    `profile_settings`, `hold_open_drafts`, `hold_programs`, `schedules`, `acceptance`, `schedule_baselines`,
    `schedule_plans`, `schedule_journal`, `schedule_operations`, `schedule_queue`, `access`.
  - Profile settings save path (`:118-129`): `save_profiles` writes into the **users store** via
    `repository.async_profile_settings(...)`; then for every user whose revision changed calls
    `manager.request_user(user.id)` (queues device sync). The separate `hikvision_intercom.profile_settings`
    store is only read once as a legacy source when the central copy is `None` (`:133-137`).
  - Hold programs (`:156-183`): `send_hold(item, command)` verifies station loaded & identity
    (`runtime.profile.unique_id == item["identity"]`) else `station_unloaded`; verifies the door/api mapping
    else `operation_unsupported`; then `hold_command(runtime.client, item["api_id"], command, commissioned=True)`
    → **PHYSICAL** (`alwaysOpen`/`close`, see client section). A timer ticks `programs.tick(now)` every **15 s**
    (`:183`), guarded by an `asyncio.Lock`.
  - Manager built with `task_factory=hass.async_create_background_task(..., eager_start=False)` (`:258-264`);
    `NativeTiming(journal, repository)` attached to `manager.engine.native_timing` when the schedule journal loaded (`:265-268`).
  - Every existing config entry registered: `manager.register(entry.entry_id, entry.title, bool(managed_locks(entry.data)))` (`:270-271`).
  - On `EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP`: stop program timer, close schedule queue, `manager.async_close()` (`:273-278`).
- `_register_services` (`:282-304`) — see services list in Storage boundary. Handler maps `AccessError` to
  `ServiceValidationError(translation_key="access_action_failed", placeholders={"reason": code})`.

**Public methods used by WS commands.** Only `get_manager` (all manager-backed commands) and `SIGNAL_ACCESS_CHANGED` (subscribe).

**Persistence.** Creates stores listed in Storage boundary (15 of the 16 `hikvision_intercom.*` keys; the 16th,
`.events`, is created in `event_manager.py:37`).

**Corrupt-storage behaviour at setup** (issue IDs are HA Repairs, severity ERROR, not fixable):
- users store corrupt → issue `users_storage_corrupt`, **re-raise → whole integration setup fails** (`:41-45`).
- `panel_permissions` corrupt → issue `panel_permissions_storage_corrupt`, `recover_from_invalid_storage()` and continue (`:57-65`).
- `appearance_settings`, `whatsapp_templates`, `ntp_settings` corrupt → object set to `None`, file preserved, no explicit issue here (the `AccessStore.async_load` itself raises `<suffix>_storage_corrupt`) (`:71-112`).
- `media_settings` → issue `media_settings_storage_corrupt`, object `None` (`:83-90`).
- `profile_settings` → issue `profile_settings_storage_corrupt`, object `None` (`:138-143`).
- `hold_open_drafts`, `hold_programs` → **no try/except**; an `AccessError` propagates and aborts setup (`:147-174`).
- `schedules`, `acceptance`, `schedule_baselines`, `schedule_plans`, `schedule_journal`, `schedule_operations` → issue `<key>_storage_corrupt`, object `None` (`:185-244`).

**Signals emitted.** `SIGNAL_ACCESS_CHANGED` (also emitted by `clock_runtime.py:61`, `event_manager.py:83`).
Listeners: `websocket.subscribe`, `sensor.IntercomSyncSensor` (`sensor.py:80`), `issues.RepairWatcher` (`issues.py:43-45`).

**Error codes raised here.** `station_unloaded`, `operation_unsupported` (hold programs).

## Module: access/manager.py (AccessManager — fleet scheduler and admin workflows)

**Responsibility.** Holds per-station runtime state (`Station`), coalesces reconciliation requests per station
into one background worker, schedules periodic/backoff re-runs, runs read-only scans, and implements the
administrator workflows (CRUD, CSV, inventory, adopt/delete-unmanaged, ignore, review/resolve).

**In-memory `Station` dataclass** (`:50-66`, not persisted):
`id` (HA config-entry id), `name` (entry title), `lock_enabled` (bool: entry has ≥1 managed lock),
`driver: AccessClient|None`, `inventory: StationInventory|None` (private full device user/card cache),
`status: str = "offline"`, `error: str|None`, `scanned_at`, `reconciled_at` (ISO UTC strings),
`scan_task`, `scan_error`, `task` (worker), `timer` (next scheduled request), `pending: bool`, `failures: int`.

Concurrency: `_read_slots = asyncio.Semaphore(3)` for scans (`:84`); engine write concurrency 3 (engine).

**Lifecycle (called by runtime, not WS).**
- `register(station_id, name, lock_enabled)` `:97-102`.
- `attach(station_id, driver)` `:104-110`: `station_already_attached` if already; sets status `"pending"`, calls `request()`. Called from `runtime.py:249` after platforms are set up.
- `async_detach(station_id)` `:112-129`: cancels enrollment/timer/worker/scan; status `"offline"`, error `"station_unloaded"`.
- `async_close()` `:131-135`: `_closed = True`; clears bulk/policy reviews; detaches all.
- Recovery trigger: `runtime.py:252-260` calls `manager.request(entry_id)` when the poll coordinator goes offline→online.

**Station sync_state values (station-level `status`)**: `offline` (initial / unloaded / connection lost),
`pending` (attached, or retry scheduled, or busy), `syncing` (worker running), `synced`, `error`.
Worker transitions (`_worker` `:251-334`):
1. Loop while `station.pending`: set `pending=False`, `status="syncing"`, `error=None`.
2. `_scan(station)` (identity + capabilities + full inventory).
3. If `engine.jobs(station.id)` non-empty: require `lock_enabled` else `station_has_no_managed_lock`;
   `result = engine.async_reconcile(station.id, _driver(station))`;
   `status = "offline" if result.offline else "error" if result.failed else "pending" if result.retry else "synced"`;
   station `error = result.last_error` only if offline ("Person failures belong to their matrix cell, not every
   station user", `:267-268`); if not offline → a second, **fresh** `_scan(station, fresh=True)` so the cached
   inventory reflects the writes. If no jobs → `status="synced"`.
4. `synced` → `reconciled_at = utc_now()`. `failures = failures+1 if retry else 0`.
5. Station-wide exceptions (`:285-314`) mark **every job user** of that station via `_mark_station` (`:192-195`,
   which calls `repository.async_mark` per user = durable storage write):
   - `HikvisionConnectionError|HikvisionTimeoutError` → retry, failures+1, `("offline","connection_failed")`.
   - `HikvisionBusyError` → retry, failures+1, `("pending","device_busy")`.
   - `HikvisionAuthError` → `("error","authentication_failed")` (no retry).
   - `HikvisionUnsupportedError` → `("error","operation_unsupported")`.
   - `AccessError` → `("error", err.code)`.
   - other `HikvisionError` → `("error", error_code(err))`.
   - any other Exception (incl. storage) → `status="error"`, `error="storage_or_internal_error"`, **break** (no per-user marks; "A storage failure must halt writes").
6. `finally` (`:318-334`): if not closed and driver attached, schedule `request(station.id)` via
   `loop.call_later(delay)`:
   - retry: `delay = min(300, 5 * 2 ** min(failures, 6))` seconds → 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 300, 300… (failures ≥1 on a retry).
   - otherwise: `delay = 300` s, possibly shortened by `timing_policy.renewal_delay(...)` (`timing_policy.py:289-318`)
     to the next HA-mode rolling validity window end (+0.1 s, min 1 s) for users with `access_timing_policy.mode == "ha"`.
   So every attached station is re-reconciled at least every 300 s even with no requests ("periodic reconciliation").

**Request/queue semantics.**
- `request(station_id)` `:149-162`: `station_not_found`, `manager_closed`. Sets `pending=True`, logs diagnostics
  `queued`, cancels the scheduled timer, starts a worker if a driver is attached and no worker is running;
  otherwise the running worker loops again. Offline/unloaded stations just keep `pending=True` (no wait). Calls `changed()`.
- `request_all()` `:180-182`: `request()` for every registered station.
- `request_user(user_id)` `:184-190`: `user_not_found` unless the id is in `users` or `tombstones`; requests
  only stations where `user_id in engine.jobs(station)`.
- `has_access(station_id)` `:164-178`: True if any binding at the station, any active user with an enabled
  assignment there, or any unconfirmed tombstone targeting it. Used by config/options flows to block
  removing the lock (`access_removal_pending`).

**Public methods used by WebSocket commands** (dispatch lines in `websocket.py`):

- `users`: `ManagedUser.public()` + `timing_readbacks: {station_id: {mode, valid_from, valid_until, revision, checked_at}}`.
  `ManagedUser.public()` = private dict minus `pin`, `cards`, `photo`, plus `photo_configured`, `pin_configured`,
  `cards: [{"id","masked_number" ("•••• " + last 4, or "••••"),"label","card_type","enabled"}]` (`access/models.py:195-204`).
  Per-user keys: `id, employee_no, display_name, phone, access_timing_draft, access_timing_policy, active, user_type,
  valid_from, valid_until, assignments{station_id: {config_entry_id, enabled, allowed_locks[], schedule_template,
  desired_revision, applied_revision, sync_state, last_sync_at, last_error}}, revision, created_at, updated_at,
  identity_locked, profile, group_ids, permission_overrides`.
- `sync_operations`: journal rows without `intent`, newest first (see sync_tracking).
- `revocations`: `[{station_id, user_id, sync_state, last_error}]` = bindings of live users at stations no longer in their assignments.
- `card_removals` / `pin_removals`: `[{id, user_id, targets, confirmed}]` (no card number / PIN).
- `tombstones`: tombstone dicts without `record`: `{user_id, employee_no, targets, confirmed, created_at, stations{sid:{sync_state,last_error}}}`.

**`async_inventory` row shape** (`:879-903`): `{"employee_no","display_name" (device name),"user_id" (bound central id or null),
"ignored","review_token" (or null),"import_error" (AccessError code or null),"pin_configured","cards":[masked card public() with random uuid ids]}`.
`import_error` comes from `_import_data` constraints (below). Calls `changed()`.

**`_import_data` constraints** (`:907-949`, used by adopt, delete_unmanaged, review, resolve, resolve_deletion):
requires managed lock (`station_offline`/`station_has_no_managed_lock`), person present (`device_user_missing`),
`RightPlan == []` (`schedule_unverified`), every `doorRight` id mapped to a managed physical lock and unique
(`unmanaged_lock`), `localUIRight is False` and `numOfFace`/`numOfFP` zero (`unsupported_credentials`),
PIN mode readable (`pin_device_managed` if `caps.pin_field is None`), validity either disabled or `timeType=="UTC"`
(`local_validity_needs_conversion`). Produces `{"employee_no","display_name","user_type","pin","valid_from","valid_until",
"cards":[{"card_no","card_type"}],"assignments":{station_id:{"allowed_locks":[physical...]}}}`.
Consequence: `users/delete_unmanaged` also refuses records with schedules, admin rights, face/fingerprint, local validity, or unmapped doors.

**Adoption semantics** (`async_adopt` + `repository.async_adopt` `repository.py:1049-1120`):
1. Validate `employee_no` (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}`); acquire station write transaction (identity re-confirmed).
2. Re-read capabilities and the single person (`async_person`), recompute fingerprint; mismatch/empty token → `review_stale`.
3. `_import_data`; unless delete, `_validate` against station capabilities.
4. Repository commit: without `user_id` → new central user from device data; with `user_id` → existing user
   (must match `revision` → else `revision_conflict`; must have same `employee_no` → else `identity_migration_required`),
   central fields kept (only the assignment is added). Assignment `{enabled: true, allowed_locks: imported}`,
   `permission_overrides[station]="allow"`, `identity_locked=True`; binding
   `{employee_no, fingerprint, intent: None, adopted: True, identity_observed_at: now}`; `already_managed` if bound.
   `delete=True` with `user_id` → `invalid_operation`. `delete=True` → immediately moves the new record into a
   tombstone `{targets:[station], confirmed:[], stations:{station:{sync_state:"delete_pending"}}, record}`.
5. `request_user(user.id)` and `changed()`.

**Ignore semantics**: `state["ignored"][station_id]` list of employee numbers; affects only `unmanaged_count`
and the inventory row flag. `invalid_boolean` if not bool.

**Conflict review** (`async_review` `:1030-1115`). Output keys:
`user_id, employee_no, station_id, review_token, revision (central or null), reviewed_at, absent, display_name,
pin_configured, cards, deletion_pending, central (public_view of desired or null), device (public_view), active,
unverified_fields (["pin"] when PIN not readable), affected_stations (sorted target station ids),
actions: {"central": {allowed, reason}, "device": {allowed, reason}, "delete": {allowed, reason}},
differences: [field labels], plan: {person: create|delete|update|none, pin: none|remove|set|change, cards_add, cards_remove, cards_update}`.
Reason codes assigned: `deletion_not_pending`, `ownership_missing` (no binding), `user_not_found` (tombstoned user
for central/device), `device_user_missing`, any `_import_data` code, any `desired_view` code, any `_validate` code.

**Conflict resolution — `direction` values**: exactly `"central"` and `"device"` (`:995-996`, else `invalid_resolution`).
Deletion is a separate command (`conflicts/resolve_deletion`), shown in review as action key `"delete"`.
- Common: current `user.revision` must equal `revision` → `revision_conflict`; under the station transaction
  re-read person, recompute fingerprint == `review_token` → `review_stale`; `_import_data` run if a device person exists.
- `central`: repository rebuilds the user with an empty patch (revision +1, same desired), rebases the binding
  (`fingerprint = device fingerprint, intent=None, sync_state="pending", last_error=None, identity_observed_at=now`)
  (`repository.py:1175-1229`). Next reconciliation then writes central desired state over the device record.
- `device`: requires device person (`device_user_missing`); device data minus `assignments` becomes the central
  desired state (name, user_type, PIN, validity, cards); removed PIN/cards are retired on all targets; binding
  rebased the same way. Next reconciliation propagates the imported values to every other assigned station.
- `resolve_deletion`: tombstone must target the station and not be confirmed (`deletion_not_pending`); token check;
  `_import_data` if a person exists; creates binding `{employee_no, fingerprint, intent:None, adopted:True,
  sync_state:"delete_pending", last_error:None}` and tombstone station state `delete_pending`
  (`repository.py:1231-1255`); then `request(station_id)`.

**`sync_diagnostics()` shape** (`:848-866`) + `websocket.py:641`:
`{"integration_version", "stations":[{"station_ref","state","last_error" (only SAFE_ERRORS else "other"),"loaded",
"managed_lock","worker_active","pending_request","reconciliation_targets"}], "retention":"last_200_stages_since_start", "recent":[rows]}`.

**Persistence.** None directly; all via `AccessRepository` (users store).

**Signals.** `self._changed()` → `SIGNAL_ACCESS_CHANGED` on nearly every state transition.

**Error codes raised in manager.py.** `station_already_attached, station_not_found, station_offline,
station_has_no_managed_lock, manager_closed, user_not_found, csv_invalid_mode, csv_duplicate_employee,
employee_conflict, csv_validation_failed, csv_review_stale, device_user_missing, schedule_unverified, unmanaged_lock,
unsupported_credentials, pin_device_managed, local_validity_needs_conversion, review_stale, invalid_boolean,
invalid_resolution, revision_conflict, deletion_not_pending`, plus pass-through `error_code(err)` values from rescan.
